description: The five numbered estimation steps in Section I.A define the statistical machinery -- the pooled population-variance estimate across the 16 paired portfolios, the t-statistic on the difference of sample means, and the separate per-month test of whether a single average residual differs from zero. Every t-statistic quoted in the results depends on these definitions, and none of them is represented in a unit.

The unit on excess volatility presents the overreaction reading without these competing explanations.

description: Table I carries per-row results that no unit represents, including the five-year formation experiment (10 replications, 50 stocks) showing a CAR difference of 0.319 at 60 months with a t-statistic of 3.28 -- the largest and most significant reversal in the paper, and stronger than the three-year result the extraction treats as headline.

The five-year experiment is explicitly framed as having the properties of a trading rule -- the average cumulative excess return before transaction costs an investor aware of the phenomenon could expect. The extraction records the persistence of the January effect from this experiment but not its economic-significance framing or the before-transaction-costs caveat.
